sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.4% a year from $38.5 billion in FY2016 to $67.6 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F201].
The path was cyclical rather than steady: a 22.4% drop in FY2020 to $41.7 billion [F5][D198] was followed by a 12.8% rise in FY2023 to $67.1 billion [F8][D357].
The FY2020 decline came from lower end-user demand and dealer inventory reductions across all three primary segments [P59].

FY2023's gain was primarily favorable price realization and higher sales volume [P32], while FY2025's 4.3% growth to $67.6 billion [F10][D463] came from higher volume partly offset by unfavorable price realization [P13].
North America supplied 54.2% of FY2025 revenue [D513] and contributed 3.4pp of growth [D515].
Power & Energy grew 11.6% in FY2025 [D758] and contributed 5.2pp [D759], with Power Generation up 32.5% [D894].
Construction Industries fell 1.6% on unfavorable price realization of $1.136 billion, partly offset by higher volume [P8][D765].
Operating income grew at a 28.6% CAGR against revenue's 6.4% [F202][F201], but FY2025 incremental operating margin was -69.1% [D488].
Diluted EPS fell 14.7% in FY2025 [D467] against a 17.7% net income decline [D465], as the diluted share count fell 3.5% [D483].
The FY2025 operating margin of 16.5% [F30] sits above the 14.3% window median but below the 20.2% FY2024 high [D1123][D1122].
The 3.7pp margin decline [D476] came from unfavorable manufacturing costs of $2.148 billion, largely tariffs, and unfavorable price realization of $817 million [P9].
Cost of revenue took 4.2pp off the margin [D490] as it rose to 66.2% of revenue from 62.0% [D441][D388].
Net margin of 13.1% [F50] trailed operating margin by 3.4pp [D1168], with a 24.0% effective tax rate [D449].
Operating cash flow of $11.7 billion was 1.32x net income in FY2025 [F80][D450], above the 1.16x window median [D1158].
Free cash flow fell 11.2% to $8.9 billion [F100][D469], a 13.2% margin [D447] below the 13.4% peer median [D1148].
Capex rose 41.9% to $2.8 billion [F90][D470], 4.2% of revenue [D446] and 1.25x D&A [D452].
Machinery, Power & Energy operating cash rose on lower working capital requirements and lower cash taxes paid [P4].
Net debt was $26.2 billion at FY2025 [D456], 38.8% of revenue [D457], with cash of $10.0 billion [F140].
That net-debt ratio ranks at the 67th percentile of three industrials peers, against a peer median of -59.4% net cash to revenue [D1169][D1170].
Total debt and net cash omit long-term debt due within one year, about $7.1 billion in FY2025 [R7][D455].
Buybacks of $5.2 billion and dividends of $2.7 billion [X140][X150] were 89.0% of free cash flow [D459], and the diluted share count fell 3.5% [D483].
The unmapped current portion of long-term debt, about $7.1 billion in FY2025, means reported total debt and net cash understate leverage every year [R7][D455].
Net debt rose for a second year, to $26.2 billion from $24.9 billion [D456][D403], on 14.1% total debt growth [D485].
FY2021-FY2025 net income in the table is proxy-sourced and differs from the 10-K by up to 0.06% [R3][F40][X20].
Operating margin: a FY2026 reading below the 14.3% window median [D1123] would confirm the tariff-driven compression, reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Capex: a ratio above the FY2025 1.25x of D&A [D452] would extend the capital build and pressure free cash flow.
Free cash flow margin: a fall below the 11.9% window median [D1129] would reverse the FY2023-FY2025 cash trend.
